verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.008868 did not improve on the current best 1.007697 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Do not enable value embeddings on every layer; the previous all-layer VE result was not a true win over the relevant max-autotune baseline.

The sliding-window-shortening line had already plateaued, so the 256->128 change was a low-EV extrapolation whose ~0.0002 expected gain was below the 0.0005 keep-threshold; pick an experiment with a realistic chance of beating the best by more than 0.0005 instead.
Do not shorten the long-range L layers to 1024; the model still needs full 2048 context in more than the final layer, so choose a non-context-sacrificing experiment instead.
Raising Muon momentum to 0.97 hurt, so the momentum knob should not have been increased; if revisiting it, test lowering the steady-state momentum instead.

The experiment was executed correctly but the hypothesis was wrong: 0.95 is already the optimal Muon momentum, and both raising and lowering it degrade val_bpb, so this hyperparameter is exhausted in both directions and a future session should target a different unexplored knob (e.g. an intermediate sliding window between 128 and 256, or a re-run of the 256→128 near-miss to rule out noise).

judge.summary: The agent reviewed the experiment history and chose to test a nonzero final learning-rate floor, changing FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1 in train.py while leaving WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.7. The motivation was that the schedule otherwise decays linearly to zero over the final 70% of the fixed budget, and a small floor might let the model continue making progress at the end. The experiment ran successfully with unchanged model size and similar memory, but produced val_bpb 1.008868, which is about 0.001171 worse than the current best 1.007697, so the run failed the improvement threshold and was not kept.
judge.feedback: The implementation was clean, but the decisive mistake was choosing a 10% final-LR floor as the experiment. That is a large perturbation to the tail of training: with WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7, the optimizer would still be at 10% of its initial LRs for a substantial final interval, effectively preventing the usual end-of-training stabilization that decaying LR to zero provides. The first error in the reasoning was not that FINAL_LR_FRAC is unsupported, but that 0.1 was an unnecessarily aggressive test of the idea. If the goal was to test whether a final LR floor can be useful, the first variant should have been much smaller, e.g. 0.01 or 0.02, so any benefit would have to appear with minimal added late-training noise before moving in the worse direction.
judge.corrected_step: FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.01     # small final LR floor if testing nonzero decay end
